The coordinator re-verified the high findings at their evidence. (1) Proposition 1.5: its proof says Gamma acts on M(mu) through mu, trivially iff mu is of Hecke character type; this fails on torsion modules, since for the golden ratio phi in Q(zeta_5), phi^3 - 1 = 2 phi, so Gamma = <phi^3> acts trivially on R/2R in the weight of one embedding, which is not of Hecke character type. (2) RS-14's reason for AutomorphicPadicLFunctions: 'own the Katz-specific ordinary deformation/lift where not supplied, differential operators, CM periods, Eisenstein measure, critical-character evaluation'. (3) Proposition 3.23: with chi_l(w) = exp(2 pi i <l, w>) and <,> = Im H, d/dz chi_l = -pi h l-bar chi_l, so the derivative carries (-1)^{|alpha|}; and dz ^ dz-bar = -2i dx ^ dy, so the measure factor is (-2i)^d, not (2i)^d. (4) Proposition 3.13: for Lambda = Z[i], K^0 = 4 zeta(s) L(s, chi_{-4}) has residue pi at s = 1 and value -1 at s = 0, while the printed residues (1 at s = 1, -1 at s = 0) are those of pi^{-s} Gamma(s) K. (5) Notation 1.18 defines R[1/f] through the maximal ideals m with m cap O_L not dividing f, for the one fixed inclusion O_L in R, so primes over conjugates of f are not inverted. (6) Katz's local factor: the TeX defines F-tilde(x, y) = chi_fin(x^{-1}, y) on (O_L(Sigma-bar) + O_L(Sigma))^x, inverting the Sigma-bar component, while (5.7.1) evaluates rho at (t^{-1}, s) and (5.4.1) puts t on O_L(Sigma_p). (7) Proposition 2.27: with Gamma = Gamma^free x Gamma^tors and the torsion central, res composed with cor on H_{d-1}(Gamma^free) is multiplication by |Gamma^tors|, so res has image |Gamma^tors| Z; for d = 1 and Gamma = {+-1}, res on H_0 is multiplication by 2. findings.claim: Proposition 1.5, copied into item 005, is false as stated: an 'algebraic T_{L,R}-module' is an arbitrary R[I_L]-comodule, and for a module with R-torsion, Γ can act trivially on M(µ) although µ(Γ) ≠ 1. The proof ('This action is trivial if and only if µ ∈ HChar_L(Γ)') needs µ(γ) − 1 to act injectively. The mistake is not recorded. Proposition 1.5 is never cited later, and Corollary 1.14 argues directly for locally free modules over the domain R ⊂ ℂ, where the argument is right. So its reach is nil, but the item as written cannot be proved.
findings.evidence: Proposition 1.5, p. 8: 'Let M be an algebraic T_{L,R}-module and suppose that R is contained in an algebraic number field k. Let Γ ⊂ O_L^× be a subgroup of finite index. Then the Γ-invariants of M are M^Γ = ⊕_{µ∈HChar_L(Γ)} M(µ). Proof. On M(µ) the group Γ ⊂ O_L^× acts via the character µ : O_L^× → R^×. This action is trivial if and only if µ ∈ HChar_L(Γ) is of Hecke character type.' Counterexample: L = ℚ(ζ_5), a CM field with L^Gal = L and d_L = 5^3. Take R = ℤ[ζ_5][1/5] ⊂ L and φ = (1+√5)/2 ∈ O_L^×. Since O_L^× = µ_10 × ⟨φ⟩, the subgroup Γ = ⟨φ^3⟩ has finite index. Let µ = σ_1 be a single embedding, and let M = R/2R with coaction m ↦ m ⊗ [σ_1]. Since φ^3 − 1 = 2φ, σ_1(γ) − 1 ∈ 2R for every γ ∈ Γ, so Γ acts trivially and M^Γ = M ≅ 𝔽_16 ≠ 0 (2 is inert in ℚ(ζ_5)). But σ_1(φ^3) = 2σ_1(φ) + 1 ≠ 1, and σ_1 fails the weight condition (µ(σ_1) + µ(σ̄_1) = 1 but µ(σ_2) + µ(σ̄_2) = 0), so σ_1 ∉ HChar_L(Γ) and the right side is 0. The label prop:decomposition is referenced nowhere in the TeX source.

findings.claim: The proof of Proposition 2.27 claims that res : H_{d−1}(Γ, Z) → H_{d−1}(Γ', Z) is surjective. This is false whenever Γ has torsion. For Γ = Γ^free × Γ^tors, the transfer composed with the inclusion H_{d−1}(Γ^free) → H_{d−1}(Γ) is multiplication by |Γ^tors|, because conjugation is trivial. The other Künneth summands are torsion and map to 0 in H_{d−1}(Γ^free) ≅ Z. So the image of res is |Γ^tors|·H_{d−1}(Γ'), and no ξ with res ξ = ξ' exists. With the normalisation forced by diagram (2.4.2) and Corollary 2.29, the map takes the inflated generator of H^{d−1}(Γ, R) to 1/|Γ^tors|. It is therefore not a homomorphism into the integral module TSym^{α+1̲}(ω_{A/R}) ⊗ TSym^β(ω_{A^∨/R}) unless |Γ^tors| ∈ R^×. If ζ_m ∈ L then the odd primes dividing m, and 2 when 4 | m, divide d_L, so they are units in an O_{L^Gal}[1/d_L]-algebra. Only a factor 2 is at stake: −1 ∈ Γ with 2 ∤ d_L. This happens for Γ = O_L^× in the f = O_L case of Theorem 4.10, and for Γ = O_f^× when f | 2 in Theorem 4.9. In those cases Definition 2.28's 'element of R' and the resulting 2-integrality are not established by the paper's argument. They may still hold for the particular classes: in d = 1 with x of order 2, the conditions Σ_t f(t) = 0 and f(t) = f(−t) force f(0) to be even, which absorbs the 1/2.

findings.claim: Item 012 is marked planned at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.2. The item also leaves out the fact the paper actually uses: after a finite extension a CM abelian variety has good reduction everywhere (Serre–Tate). That fact gives Theorem 4.10's 'Moreover, one can choose Spec R = Spec O_k[1/(d_L𝔣N𝔠)]' and hence the ring in the Introduction's main theorem. No item states it and no stage plans it. Item 060 also repeats Remark 4.4 ('such 𝒜 exist over number fields since ℂ^Σ/𝔞 has CM by 𝒪_L') with status missing, while 012 marks the same remark planned. That is the Serre–Tate theorem that abelian varieties with complex multiplication have potentially good reduction everywhere. findings.claim: Item 039 copies the printed definition L^1_R := ker(N_{L/Q} : (R⊗L)^× → R^×). For totally imaginary L this group is {z ∈ (C^×)^Σ : ∏|z_σ|^2 = 1} ≅ (S^1)^d × R^{d−1}, which is not contractible. Γ'\L^1_R is then a compact (2d−1)-torus, with H_{d−1} ≅ Z^{binom(2d−1, d−1)} (Z^3 for d = 2). So the asserted isomorphisms Z ≅ H_{d−1}(Γ'\L^1_R, Z) ≅ H_{d−1}(Γ', Z) are false for d ≥ 2. The intended object is the positive model of §3.2. The orientation is also not determined: the complex orientation of R⊗L ≅ C^Σ does not depend on any ordering of Σ, and the statement does not say how an orientation passes to the hypersurface. The sign of every EK^{β,α} depends on this orientation. Also: Proposition 2.27, as quoted in item 039, orients L^1_R = ker(N : (R (x) L)^x -> R^x) and claims Z = H_{d-1}(Gamma'\L^1_R, Z) = H_{d-1}(Gamma', Z). For L totally imaginary, this kernel has real dimension 2d-1 and is (S^1)^Sigma x {r : prod r = 1}. It is not contractible, Gamma'\L^1_R is homotopy equivalent to a (2d-1)-torus, and H_{d-1} has rank binom(2d-1, d-1), which is 3 for d = 2. The space that works is the image {r in R^Sigma_{>0} : prod r = 1} under x -> (|sigma(x)|^2), which is the E Gamma of Section 3.2 that Theorem 3.27 integrates over. The orientation 'on R (x) L' induced by an ordering of Sigma is the complex orientation of C^Sigma, which does not depend on the ordering. So it cannot cancel the ordering-dependent sign of omega^d = TSym^1 omega, and the claimed independence of the ordering needs the log-coordinate orientation of the hyperplane. Its convention, coordinates (r_1, ..., r_{d-1}) or a normal-first boundary orientation, which differ by (-1)^{d-1}, decides the sign (-1)^{d(d-1)/2} of Theorem 3.27.

R^dπ_*(P^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) → R^dπ_*(P^{(0)} ⊗ Ω^d) = R^dπ_*Ω^d is an isomorphism for every n (base change gives R^dπ_*P^{(n)} = Tor_0 ⊗ ω^{−d}_{A^∨}); γ_# is the identity on P^{(0)} = O_A; and the trace is invariant under automorphisms. findings.claim: Definition 3.24, and item 054, define E^{beta,alpha}(t',s;Lambda,Gamma) for Re s > (b-a)/2 + d. For an infinity type of Hecke character type, beta_i - alpha_i = w for all i, so |summand| = N(lambda)^{w/2 - Re s}. A lattice coset modulo units then gives absolute convergence exactly for Re s > 1 + w/2 = 1 + (b-a)/(2d). This is also what the paper's own K-series bound gives for K^{beta+alpha}(Hr,t,0,a+ds) in Lemma 3.26. The printed half-plane is smaller than the correct one when w >= -2, but for d >= 2 and w < -2 it contains points of divergence.
findings.evidence: Definition 3.24, p. 43: 's in C with Re(s) > (b-a)/2 + d'. Section 3.3, p. 35: K^mu converges for 'Re s > d + |mu|/2'. With mu = beta + alpha and argument a + ds this is Re s > 1 + (b-a)/(2d). Example: d = 2, a quartic CM field, beta = 0, alpha = (5,5), w = -5. The printed condition allows s = -2 > -3, where the terms have absolute value N(lambda)^{-1/2} and the series diverges, since convergence needs an exponent > 1.
findings.fix: Change the half-plane in item 054 to Re s > 1 + (b-a)/(2d) and record the misstatement as a sourceIssue. It affects nothing later, because only the analytic continuation at s = 0 is used.

findings.claim: The proof of (A.2.1) in Appendix A.2 claims that Ĩ = q^Γ_*p^{-1}I is flabby for every injective Γ-equivariant I. That is false, and so is the step behind it, Γ(U, Ĩ) ≅ Γ(p(q^{-1}(U)), I)^Γ, which needs connected fibres of q^{-1}(U) → p(q^{-1}(U)). /030 copies 'ℐ̃ is flabby for injective Γ-equivariant ℐ' into its statement. The isomorphism (A.2.1) is still true, but needs another argument.
findings.evidence: Appendix A.2, p. 81: 'To show that the derived functors coincide, it remains to see that Ĩ is flabby on EΓ×_Γ X for an injective Γ-equivariant sheaf I on X' and 'Γ(U, Ĩ) ≅ Γ(q^{-1}(U), p^{-1}I)^Γ ≅ Γ(p(q^{-1}(U)), I)^Γ because p is an open map'. Counterexample: X = point, Γ = ℤ and I = Hom_ℤ(ℤ[Γ], ℚ/ℤ), which is an injective ℤ[Γ]-module with I^Γ ≅ ℚ/ℤ ≠ I. Then EΓ×_Γ X = S^1 and Ĩ is the local system of I. For an arc U, q^{-1}(U) is a disjoint union of translates, so Γ(U, Ĩ) ≅ I while Γ(p(q^{-1}U), I)^Γ = I^Γ. Restriction Γ(S^1, Ĩ) = I^Γ → Γ(U, Ĩ) = I is not surjective, so Ĩ is not flabby; it is only acyclic, since H^1(S^1, Ĩ) = H^1(ℤ, I) = 0. The same page also has a misprint: 'Γ(V, Ĩ)^Γ ≅ Hom_Γ(j_!ℤ, I)' should be Γ(V, I)^Γ, because V ⊂ X.
findings.fix: Delete the flabbiness clause from /030 and give a correct proof route. Compare the spectral sequence H^p(Γ, H^q(X,ℱ)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X,Γ;ℱ) with the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence H^p(Γ, H^q(EΓ×X, p^{-1}ℱ)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(EΓ×_Γ X, ℱ̃) for the free, properly discontinuous action. p^* is an isomorphism on E_2 by homotopy invariance, since EΓ is contractible. Equivalently, show that Ĩ is acyclic. Record a sourceIssue with kind error, locator 'Appendix A.2, proof of (A.2.1), p. 81' and affects 'the proof', together with the misprint Γ(V, Ĩ)^Γ → Γ(V, I)^Γ.

findings.claim: The item, following the paper, says that for Σ lifted from K, (ORD-p) 'means' that every prime of F over p splits in K. Splitting is necessary but not sufficient. When a prime of K above p has several inducing embeddings, a CM type can contain embeddings inducing both 𝔓 and 𝔓̄. Correct statement: Σ is p-ordinary iff every prime of F over p splits in K and, for each prime 𝔓 | p of K, the embeddings inducing 𝔓 lie all in Σ_K or all in Σ̄_K. Splitting is equivalent to the existence of some p-ordinary CM type.
findings.evidence: §5.1, p. 56: 'If Σ is lifted from a CM field K with maximal totally real subfield F, then the condition (ORD-p) means that all primes in F over p split completely in K.' Counterexample: K = ℚ(ζ_8), F = ℚ(√2), p = 5. Here 5 is inert in F because (2/5) = −1, and (5) splits in K because 5 has order 2 in (ℤ/8)^×. Write a for the embedding ζ ↦ ζ^a; the decomposition group is {1, 5}, so a = 1 and a = 5 induce 𝔓 while a = 3 and a = 7 induce 𝔓̄. The CM type Σ = {1, 3} (one from each conjugate pair {1,7}, {3,5}) has Σ_p = {𝔓, 𝔓̄} = Σ̄_p, so it is not p-ordinary.
findings.fix: In item 069 replace 'means that every prime … splits in K' with the correct criterion above, and note that splitting is only necessary (it is equivalent to existence). Add a sourceIssue (error; locator §5.1, p. 56; affects: nothing, since the paper only ever assumes (ORD-p) itself).

findings.claim: Mathlib's abstract-measure carrier D(X, R) is defined for any topological space X, so measures on O_L ⊗ Z_p already have a library carrier, and Mathlib has the Amice transform. The extraction cites only the Mahler basis, which invites a parallel measure carrier in the Part II (items 079, 081, 084). Also: The library notes miss two relevant Mathlib APIs at the pinned commit. (1) The abstract Mellin functional-equation package WeakFEPair. Item 047's theta transformation makes (t -> theta^mu_t(H,z,w,Lambda), t -> theta^mu_t(H,w,z,Lambda^*)) such a pair, with weight k = d + |mu| and root number e^{2 pi i<w,z>}/vol_H(Lambda). Mathlib then gives the continuation, the functional equation and the residues of the completed function. (2) Distributions on open subsets of finite-dimensional real spaces, with the Dirac delta and derivatives: the local building blocks for the currents of item 045 and the delta_t of item 051. Currents on manifolds and on tori are still missing, so the statuses stay missing. Also: The note says 'Neither local cohomology of O-modules nor the local Ext computation is in the libraries'. Mathlib defines local cohomology of R-modules exactly as the colimit of Ext over powers of an ideal, which is the affine case of SGA 2's formula. Four accepted extractions mark that statement library. Also: The items use CM fields and 'the maximal CM field K ⊂ L' but never cite Mathlib's CM-field carrier, which the reviewed library audit records.
